_comment: Inert-utility allowlist (issue #556). Each entry WAS a file mapped to the text-*/bg-*/border-* utilities in it that Tailwind compiles to NOTHING — they emit no CSS, so the styling is silently absent. They were BUGS, not exemptions: each one a near-miss of a real token, so fixing them is a behaviour change (styling appears where it was previously absent) and belonged in its own change rather than the one that introduced the guard. 🟢 THE LIST IS NOW EMPTY (issue #563), which is the strongest state it can be in: the rail's skip predicate is `allow[file]?.includes(base)`, so with nothing listed EVERY inert utility in web/src is a failure and the rail enforces at zero everywhere. That also closes the loophole #563 measured — the ratchet was keyed on the (file, utility) PAIR with no count, so `border-outline-var` grew 3 → 9 inside an already-listed file while CI stayed green. An empty list has no pair to grow behind. The list may only SHRINK, and it has no room left to: a new entry here is a regression, not a deferral. Fixed: border-outline-var -> border-outline-variant; text-on-surface-variant -> text-on-surface-var; text-negative -> text-danger; text-positive -> text-ok; bg-surface-2 / bg-surface-container-high -> bg-surface-high (both sites sit on bg-surface-container, and 25 other hovers on that exact base already resolve to surface-high).
